# Tridactyle tridactylites (Rolfe) Schltr.

First published in Beih. Bot. Centralbl., Abt. 2. 36: 148 (1918)

This species is accepted

The native range of this species is Tropical Africa. It is an epiphytic subshrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

### According to GrassBase - The Online World Grass Flora

Morphology General Habit
    Perennial; caespitose; clumped densely. Rootstock evident. Culms geniculately ascending; 10-90 cm long; wiry. Culm-internodes distally glabrous, or pilose. Culm-nodes pubescent. Leaf-sheaths glabrous on surface, or pilose. Ligule a fringe of hairs; 0.4-1 mm long.     Europe: southeastern. Africa: north, Macaronesia, northeast tropical, and east tropical. Asia-temperate: western Asia and Arabia. Asia-tropical: India.
Reference
    Paniceae. FTEA.
[GB]

### According to Flora of Tropical East Africa

Gramineae, W. D. Clayton, S. M. Phillips & S. A. Renvoize. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1974

Morphology General Habit
    Perennial, forming tussocks from a woody rootstock; culms 10–60 cm. high, ascending, wiry with narrow leaves or herbaceous and leafy.
Morphology Leaves
    Leaf-blades flat or involute, 2–15 cm. long, 1–5 mm. wide.
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences
    Panicle usually narrowly oblong, 3–15 cm. long, fairly dense.
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences Spikelets
    Spikelets 2.5–3.5 mm. long; lower glume a tiny truncate scale (rarely up to 0.5 mm.); upper glume ovate, tuberculate-pilose with white hairs extending 0.5–4 mm. beyond the tip but often giabrous on the upper 1/4, acute and usually mucronate; lower lemma resembling the upper glume.
Habitat
    Dry stony hills, often in crevices between boulders; 200–2800 m.
Distribution
    K1 K2 K3 K4 K6 K7 T1 T2 T3 U1 extends northwards to the Mediterraneanthence westwards to Canary and Cape Verde Is., and eastwards to India
[FTEA]

### According to Flora of Oman

Shahina Agha Ghazanfar (2018). Flora of the Sultanate of Oman. Volume 4. Hydrocharitaceae - Orchidaceae. – Meise, Botanic Garden Meise.

Morphology General Habit
    Perennial, forming tussocks from a woody rootstock, up to 60 cm high, ascending, the culms wiry with narrow leaf-blades or herbaceous and leafy; leaf-blades rigid, glaucous, flat or inrolled, glabrous or thinly pubescent; ligule a line of hairs
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences
    Panicle usually narrowly oblong, 3–15 cm long, fairly dense
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences Spikelets
    Spikelets 2.5–3.5 mm long; lower glume a minute truncate scale (rarely up to 0.5 mm); upper glume ovate, tuberculate-pilose with white hairs extending 0.5–4 mm beyond the tip, but often glabrous in the upper quarter, acute and usually mucronate.
